Subject: Re: Clarify: capacity lift vs. feature-bundle upgrade (credits & rollback)

Claire — appreciate the clear asks. Summary below, plus attached spreadsheet with two modeled scenarios (lift-only vs bundle). High-level: 

- Capacity lift (throughput/seat increase): immediate billing for the incremental committed capacity; we apply a proportional credit for unused portion if you downgrade within the first billing cycle only. After the first 30 days, downgrades are handled on a 30-day notice and we issue account credits (not cash refunds) prorated to unused commitment.

- Feature bundle (monitoring + long-retention + 24x7 support): billed as an addon line item. If you upgrade to bundle and then cancel within the pilot window (60 days), we offer a one-time credit equal to 50% of the bundle fee for the remainder of the term, provided usage is within the modeled thresholds.

- Hybrid path we recommend: provision a temporary committed lift for the pilot (60 days) + enable bundle as a 30-day trial. If you proceed to full commit, we apply a sign-up credit (shown in tab "Commit Credits") against the first 3 months. This minimizes churn risk and keeps monthly invoices predictable.

Next steps: Ben — can you confirm the promotional credit % we can extend for WellSpan (they're at the threshold for our mid-market protected discount)? Jordan — confirm the technical gating for retention toggle (can it be turned off without data loss in rollback?).

Attached: wellspan-pricing-scenarios.xlsx (two tabs: "LiftOnly" and "Lift+Bundle")

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Claire Holmes <claire.holmes@wellspan.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: capacity lift vs. feature-bundle upgrade (credits & rollback)

Thanks Marissa. Per internal promo matrix, we can extend a one-time onboarding credit equal to 20% of the first 3 months' committed lift value for WellSpan (applies to committed throughput only). For bundles, we can offer a 15% first-term discount (applies to addon fee) if they sign amendment within 14 days of pilot start.

Two constraints to call out: promo credits are non-refundable and cannot be stacked with enterprise-level volume discounts. If procurement pushes for cash refunds on rollback, legal will push back — we should keep to credits + prorations.

Ben
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Claire Holmes <claire.holmes@wellspan.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify: capacity lift vs. feature-bundle upgrade (credits & rollback)

Claire — quick tech note on rollback: retention toggles are reversible but long-retention export takes up to 48 hours to stage. If you disable the addon during a rollback, data remains accessible for 30 days in a read-only export bucket; after that the standard retention rules apply. No data loss in the 60-day pilot rollback window. For throughput rollback, we snapshot KV caches and gracefully drain existing in-flight sessions to avoid token loss — customers see a short warmup period post-downgrade.

I'll flag the retention export workflow in the amendment language to make procurement comfortable.

Jordan
Lead Solutions Architect

Claire
